name: Qthemy Slider Builder
author: Qthemy

sections.description:
Qthemy Slider Builder lets you create sliders directly from your WordPress dashboard using a visual, layer-based editor. Every feature in this plugin is free and works without a license key or an account. It connects to qthemy.com only for the template library, when you open the Templates page or the Sliders page (see External Services).

No page-builder plugin is required. Create as many sliders, slides, and layers as you need.

Features

Visual slider editor
Add, arrange, and resize elements directly on a live preview of each slide, with rulers and draggable alignment guides.

Sliders page
Your sliders as cards with a live preview of their first slide, their status, and a shortcode you copy with one click. Search and filter them, start a new one from a blank slider, a template, or a file, and duplicate, export, or move a slider to the Trash from its card.

Template library
Ready-made sliders for every screen size, with a live preview on desktop, tablet, and mobile. Filter them by language (templates designed in Arabic or in English), category, and Free or Pro. Import a free template with one click: it is added as a draft slider and its images are added to your Media Library. Pro templates are marked as such and need the Pro add-on with an active license.

Content protection
Turn on “Protect content” for a slider, and visitors cannot right-click it, select and copy its text, or drag and save its pictures (it is on for new sliders). Pictures are never picked up by a mouse swipe.

Heading, text editor, image, button, shape, and rating elements
Headings fit their text (press Enter for a new line) and take an HTML tag (H1-H6 or paragraph) for SEO. The text editor element writes paragraphs with a toolbar like the WordPress editor: bold, italic, underline, strikethrough, bulleted and numbered lists, links, text color, and highlight; pasted text keeps only that simple formatting. Add images with alt text and opacity, buttons sized by their inner spacing with an optional icon, shapes (rectangle, circle, triangle, diamond, pentagon, hexagon, octagon, star, parallelogram) with a border that keep their proportions on every device, and star ratings with half stars that fill from the right on right-to-left sites, with an optional shine, pulse, or twinkle motion. Any element can be duplicated from the layers list.

Carousel element
Put a carousel of images and videos inside a slide, next to your heading and buttons. Choose the cards from the Media Library, give each one an optional caption and link, and pick a look: a moving row (one card at a time, with optional arrows and dots) or a continuous strip (with a gap of 0 it becomes a filmstrip). Set how many cards show on each device, the gap, the card ratio (1:1, 4:5, 3:4, or 16:9), and the corners. It plays on its own and follows a mouse or finger drag; it waits while it is out of view, when the visitor’s device asks for less motion, or while someone moves through it with the keyboard. A video plays only while its card shows, and on right-to-left sites the cards move from the right. The Pro add-on adds four more looks.

Container (Flex and Grid)
Group elements in a container and they arrange themselves: in a row or a column (with wrapping, distribution, and alignment) or in a grid with a set number of columns. Every layout setting, the gap, and the inner spacing can differ per device, for example three columns on desktop and one on mobile. Drag elements into a container, reorder them inside it, or drag them out. Let the container set the width of its elements (equal shares of a row, the full width of a column or cell), and give it a background image, a shadow, and a blur behind it.

Typography
Every element with text gets the same settings: size, weight, line height, and letter spacing. Text uses your theme’s font, so sliders match the rest of your site.

Sizes that fit smaller screens
Font sizes and button spacing shrink on their own on laptop, tablet, and mobile (80%, 67%, and 53% of desktop) until you set a size for that device.

Content, Style, and Advanced tabs
Element settings are grouped into three tabs, so the setting you need is always easy to find.

Device visibility
Hide any element on desktop, laptop, tablet, or mobile.

Per-device layouts
Set the position, size, font size, and text alignment of every element separately for Desktop, Laptop, Tablet, and Mobile, and choose a slider width and height for each device.

Slide backgrounds
Use a solid color, a gradient, or an image from the Media Library, with an optional color or gradient overlay. Give the slider rounded corners, set for each corner, and a shape on its top or bottom edge (wave, waves, curve, tilt, triangle, mountains, zigzag, arrow, or bumps) in the color of the page around it.

Color picker with gradients
Every color opens one picker with HEX, an opacity bar, ready-made colors, and an eyedropper. Slide backgrounds, text, button backgrounds, and shapes also get a Gradient tab (linear or radial, two colors, angle).

Autoplay and navigation
Slides can play automatically with your own slide time. Visitors can also move between slides with arrows, dots, or by swiping, with a smooth fade transition. Place the arrows in the bottom bar or on the sides, choose line or round dots, and pick their color.

Slider width
Keep the slider at the size you set, stretch it to the width of its container, or stretch it to the full width of the screen. In the wide modes the background fills the width while the elements stay centered, also when a page builder container changes the slider’s width. Inside Elementor containers the slider takes the container’s width automatically.

Fast loading
Images of the other slides load only when they are about to be shown.

Duplicate, export, and import
Duplicate a slider, export it as a ZIP file with its images, and import it on another site, where the images are added to the Media Library. Files exported as .json by earlier versions can still be imported.

Block, Elementor widget, and shortcode
Add a slider with the “Qthemy Slider” block in the block editor or the “Qthemy Slider” widget in Elementor (in the “Qthemy” tab of its panel), or use the [qthemy_slider id="123"] shortcode anywhere else.

Arabic and English editor
Switch the editor interface between Arabic (right-to-left) and English.

Optional add-on

A separate, paid add-on, Qthemy Slider Builder Pro, is available from qthemy.com/slider-builder. It is not required, and it is not included in this plugin. It adds over 100 Google Fonts (more than 30 Arabic) stored on your own site, text effects (italic, letter case, underline, shadow, outlined text, balanced lines), icon, social-media, countdown, animated text, number counter, before/after, video (Media Library, YouTube, or Vimeo), bullet list, and badge elements, element animations with a timeline, additional slide transitions, autoplay extras (play/pause button, progress bar, per-slide timing), video backgrounds, and Ken Burns motion for image backgrounds.

While the add-on is not installed, the editor’s Elements tab lists the names of its elements in a separate section with a “Learn more” link. You can hide that section with one click.

Source Code

All JavaScript and CSS files in this plugin are the original, human-readable source code. They are not compiled, bundled, or minified, and no build tools or build step are used:

  • assets/admin/js/admin-builder.js – the visual slider editor
  • assets/admin/js/dashboard.js – the Sliders page and the Templates page
  • assets/admin/js/admin-notice.js – remembers when the add-on notice is dismissed
  • assets/admin/js/block.js – the “Qthemy Slider” block for the block editor
  • assets/admin/js/elementor-editor.js – the “More Qthemy plugins” link in the Elementor panel
  • assets/admin/js/list-actions.js – the “Import” button on the sliders list
  • assets/frontend/js/frontend.js – the front-end slider
  • assets/admin/css/admin-builder.css, assets/admin/css/dashboard.css, and assets/frontend/css/frontend.css – styles

You can read and modify these files directly.

Developer Notes

Add-ons can extend the plugin without modifying it:

  • Front end: window.QthemySB.registerLayerType(), registerBackgroundType(), and addLayerDecorator(), plus the qthemy-sb:beforeinit (bubbles to the document), qthemy-sb:ready, qthemy-sb:beforechange, qthemy-sb:change, qthemy-sb:autoplay, and qthemy-sb:userinteract events on each slider element.
  • Editor: define window.QthemySBBuilderExtension (documented at the top of assets/admin/js/admin-builder.js).
  • PHP: the qthemy_sb_render_config and qthemy_sb_sanitize_data filters and the qthemy_sb_frontend_assets_enqueued action.
  • Template library: the qthemy_sb_templates_api filter (or the QTHEMY_SB_TEMPLATES_API constant) points the library at another address, and the qthemy_sb_template_license filter lets an add-on add its license details to requests for Pro templates.

External Services

Qthemy template library:

The Templates page and the “Start from a template” part of the Sliders page show ready-made sliders from the Qthemy template library on qthemy.com.

  • What it is used for: listing the templates, showing a live preview of one, and importing it as a new slider.
  • What is sent and when: when an administrator opens one of these pages, your site’s server requests the list of templates from https://qthemy.com/wp-json/qthemy/v1/slider-templates and keeps it for 12 hours. When an administrator previews or imports a template, the server requests that template, and an import also downloads the template’s images. These requests name only the template asked for and, like every request WordPress sends, carry your site’s address and your server’s IP address. For a Pro template, the Qthemy Slider Builder Pro add-on (when it is installed with an active license) adds its product name, license key, your site’s domain, and its version, which qthemy.com checks with the Qthemy license service.
  • The administrator’s browser loads the templates’ cover images, a template’s short preview video while the pointer is on its cover (or in the preview of a Pro template without a license), and the images of a previewed template, directly from qthemy.com.
  • Nothing is requested on the pages your visitors see, and no data about your visitors or your sliders is sent.
  • The service is operated by Qthemy. Terms: https://qthemy.com/terms-and-conditions/ Privacy policy: https://qthemy.com/privacy-policy/
sections.installation:
1. Upload the qthemy-slider-builder folder to /wp-content/plugins/, or install the plugin from the Plugins screen.
  2. Activate the plugin through the Plugins screen in WordPress.
  3. Go to Slider Builder → Add New to create your first slider, then click Publish.
  4. Add the “Qthemy Slider” block (or the Elementor widget) to a page and choose your slider. You can also paste the shortcode from the Sliders list.
sections.faq:
Does Qthemy Slider Builder require Elementor or another page builder?

No. The plugin includes its own visual editor. If you use Elementor, a “Qthemy Slider” widget is included.

How do I add a slider to a page?

Publish the slider, then add the “Qthemy Slider” block (block editor) or widget (Elementor) and choose the slider. The shortcode from the Sliders list works everywhere else.

Does the plugin connect to any external service?

Only for the template library on qthemy.com, and only in the dashboard: when you open the Templates page or the Sliders page, and when you preview or import a template. Your sliders run on your own site, and your visitors only load files from it. See External Services.

Where can I find the source code?

See the “Source Code” section below.
sections.changelog:
1.6.0

  • New Carousel element: images and videos that move inside a slide, each card with an optional caption and link. Two looks: a moving row with optional arrows and dots, and a continuous strip. Set the cards shown on each device, the gap, the card ratio, and the corners, plus autoplay speed and direction, loop, pause on hover, and drag. A card that goes round to the other end comes back in from the edge, never across the other cards.
  • The carousel waits while it is out of view, when the visitor’s device asks for less motion, or while someone moves through it with the keyboard. A video plays only while its card shows.
  • The carousel’s script loads only on pages whose slider has a carousel.

1.5.0

  • New Sliders page, the plugin’s home (“All Sliders”): your sliders as cards with a live picture of their first slide, their status, and a shortcode you copy with one click. Search and filter them, and edit, duplicate, export, or move a slider to the Trash (with Undo) from its card. Point at a card’s picture to open the editor. The WordPress table is one link away.
  • New template library: ready-made sliders from qthemy.com with a live preview on desktop, tablet, and mobile, and a short video of a template playing when the pointer is on its cover. Filter them by Free or Pro, by language (designed in Arabic or in English), and by category, then import one as a draft slider; its images are added to your Media Library. Pro templates need the Pro add-on with an active license. A template made with a newer version asks you to update the plugin first.
  • Export is now a ZIP file with the slider and its images. Import takes the ZIP or a .json file from earlier versions, and an image imported before is reused, not copied again.
  • New “Protect content” switch (Playback & Navigation, on for new sliders): visitors cannot right-click the slider, select and copy its text, or drag and save its pictures. Pictures in a slider are never picked up by a mouse swipe.
  • Preview: the window keeps one size and shows only the slider, with no white space around it, also for a height in %. It opens on the slide you are editing, with Replay, Whole screen, and Landscape (tablet and phone) buttons.
  • Fixed: the small size bar that shows on scroll kept the old height. Switching the height unit now converts the number (600px is 67% of a 900px screen).
  • New “Upgrade to Pro” page with the Pro features and a Free vs Pro table.
  • Arabic translation updated. Imported ZIP files are checked for their number of files and the size of each one.

1.4.0

  • Container: a new “Element width” setting. With “Fill the container”, headings, text, images, and buttons take their width from the container: equal shares of a row, or the full width of a column or a grid cell.
  • Container: a background image under its color, shadow levels (soft, medium, strong), and a blur behind it.
  • Container: drag its handle down to make it taller.
  • Container: the “+” box after its elements is gone. When the first element goes in, a short note under the container says you can drag more elements into it; it closes after 3 seconds.
  • Container: distribution and alignment buttons show the real direction (left, center, right; top, middle, bottom) and follow the container’s row or column. The separate “Order starts” setting is gone.
  • Fixed: resizing an element inside a container moved it out of the container. It now grows and shrinks inside it, up to the container’s width.
  • Fixed: “Full cell width” in a grid container now shows in the editor too.
  • Editor: images no longer flash after moving an element. The preview window shows a loading mark instead of a blank page, no longer flickers on desktop, and takes the right height for each device.
  • Editor: the selected element stands out in the layers list, which scrolls to it. The settings board above the slide leaves no empty space on any screen size: the slides list is wider and fills its column, and the slider shape card spans under playback and transitions.
  • Elementor: the “Qthemy Slider” widget is in a “Qthemy” tab of the Elementor panel, shared with other Qthemy plugins, with a “More Qthemy plugins” link for administrators.

1.3.1

  • Fonts and text effects (italic, letter case, underline or strikethrough, text shadow, outlined text, balanced lines) are now part of the Pro add-on. Text uses your theme’s font; size, weight, line height, and letter spacing stay in this plugin. Sliders keep their settings, and with the add-on they look as before.
  • Font weight offers Light, Medium, and Heavy, the weights that look right in theme fonts. New headings and buttons start at Heavy; existing elements keep their weight.
  • The plugin no longer connects to any outside service.
  • Add-ons can add typography settings to the editor and the front end.
  • Copyright notice in the plugin files.

1.3.0

  • New Text editor element: paragraphs with bold, italic, underline, strikethrough, bulleted and numbered lists, links, text color, and highlight.
  • New Container element: arrange elements in a row, a column, or a grid, with its own settings for each device. Drag elements in, reorder them, or drag them out. A container cannot go inside another container.
  • Headings fit their text, and Enter starts a new line.
  • Fonts and typography for every element with text: over 100 Google Fonts (more than 30 Arabic), stored on your own site, plus italic, letter case, underline or strikethrough, line height, letter spacing, text shadow, outlined text, and balanced lines.
  • Font sizes and button spacing shrink on laptop, tablet, and mobile until you set a size for that device.
  • Buttons are sized by their inner spacing (each side, each device) and font size, with an automatic or fixed width. Existing buttons keep their size.
  • The color picker has an opacity bar, which replaces the separate opacity fields. Existing values are kept.
  • Corners can be set for each device.
  • Shapes keep their proportions on every device. New shapes start square.
  • The slider can have a shape on its top or bottom edge.
  • Star ratings can shine, pulse, or twinkle.
  • Any element can be duplicated from the layers list.
  • Editor: drag elements from the Elements tab onto the slide, snapping guides while moving, a compact bar with the devices and slides while you scroll, and a tidier settings board.
  • Editor: while the Pro add-on is not installed, the Elements tab lists its elements by name. The section can be hidden.
  • Deleting the plugin now removes the fonts it downloaded. Sliders are kept.
  • Fixed: button text and icons shrink with a slider shown narrower than its design, and theme link styles no longer change slider buttons.
  • Security: extra checks on values the editor puts into styles.
  • Revised Arabic interface text.

1.2.1

  • New sliders start at common screen sizes: 1920 × 700 on desktop, 1366 × 600 on laptops, 768 × 600 on tablets, and 390 × 560 on phones. Existing sliders keep their sizes.
  • An element hidden on the device you are editing is now shown in grey with stripes and a “Hidden on” label, so it is clear it will not appear there.

1.2.0

  • Added rounded corners for the slider, set for each corner.
  • Added a gradient option for the slide overlay color.
  • Added opacity for image elements.
  • The “container width” layout now fills Elementor containers and keeps elements centered when the container width changes.

1.1.1

  • Add-ons can mark their own element types as read-only in the editor.

1.1.0

  • Renamed the plugin to Qthemy Slider Builder.
  • Added button icons.
  • Added autoplay with a custom slide time.
  • Added a documented extension API for add-ons.
  • Added shape (nine outlines) and star rating elements.
  • Added HTML tags (H1-H6, paragraph) and letter spacing for text, and alt text for images.
  • Added Content, Style, and Advanced tabs to element settings.
  • Added per-device element visibility.
  • Added gradients to the color picker for slide backgrounds, text, buttons, and shapes.
  • Added a block for the block editor and an Elementor widget.
  • Added slider duplicate, export, and import.
  • Added container-width and screen-width slider layouts.
  • Added arrow position, dot shape, and navigation color options.
  • Images of the other slides now load only when needed.

1.0.27

  • Updated the admin-menu icon.

1.0.1

  • First public release.
